records.region: Imperial Valley and Salton Sea, southeastern California, United States.
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded named downstream river-component candidate only. Not a representative whole-system identity for the desert, managed drainage and lake-interior object.
records.material_pending_reason: Sources do not establish the chosen eastern desert opening and All-American Canal approach, the long East Mesa transfer into the East Highline/agricultural grid, or the particular lower managed-pond through-connection into the lake.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This selection includes an eastern desert/managed-water approach, Holtville Main Drain, part of Alamo River, and a long ending within Salton Sea. It is not the full Alamo River from its border-area source and is not New River.
records.completion_scope: All 34 stored parts and all joins were considered against three original overlapping map views, including original crop inspection at the opening, agricultural-drain junction, side-lake corridor and delta. Independent regional prose was read. The named downstream components and actual interior-lake ending are supported; specific eastern and managed through-links remain unestablished.
records.supported_name_scope: Selected mapped Alamo River corridor downstream of the Holtville Main Drain junction toward the lower delta; excludes the eastern desert opening, the separately named drain and the long Salton Sea interior continuation.

scope_limits: A visible nearby canal or broadly shared receiving basin does not establish the long selected East Mesa waterway.
The source distinguishes river, drain, side lakes, managed ponds and receiving lake. Current operating transfers or exact name boundaries are unverified.
The source map supports the actual endpoint within Salton Sea at reference-map scope, without a current shoreline claim.
Alamo River is not extended as a scalar name to the whole modeled object.

records.region: Meseta de Somuncurá–Valcheta–Curicó basin, Río Negro, Argentina
records.candidate_name_role: Regional middle/lower reach candidate; not a supported whole-selected-system identity
records.material_pending_reason: The independent original management-plan maps are readable as regional cartography but their pale, generalized drainage does not establish the substantial plateau-to-spring approach, every middle-course through-link, or the selected continuation north of the prominent lake cluster into its actual internal endpoint. The independently identified biological thesis could not be read after an anti-bot challenge. These are genuine missing correspondence links, not a completed no-name or scalar-scope decision.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This is the inland Somuncurá–Valcheta setting, not the Río Negro river mainstem. The successfully inspected plan explicitly distinguishes Curicó-basin Valcheta, Chasicó and Paja Alta from the neighboring Indio Muerto and other drainage groups. The selected terminal was not replaced with the nearest named lagoon or a generic endorheic-basin label.
records.completion_scope: A bounded source-correspondence investigation was performed for the sole fragment and all 26 stored parts. Regional identity and landscape were established, but whole-path correspondence remains incomplete. Ordinary corridor and connector evidence, rather than exact banks or individual model vertices, is what remains missing.
records.supported_name_scope: Named regional watercourse and basin relationship only; precise selected reach limits remain unassigned.

scope_limits: Whether the substantial modeled plateau opening is an ordinary natural drainage linked to the named spring-fed Valcheta reaches.
Which selected intermediate feeders and joins correspond to Brazo Frío, Brazo Caliente or other local channels, if any.
Which individual lake or depression passages the lower selection follows and whether the last northern leg is a natural through-link.
The geographic identity of the actual internal endpoint, and whether the name Valcheta applies beyond any particular lake entry or shore-side passage.
Current flow, irrigation operation, water level and precise shoreline position are not established by the historical management plan.

records.region: Nevada, United States: northern Ione Valley, Ione Wash, Millers plain and playas southwest of McLeans
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded mapped middle/lower wash candidate; not a completed representative identity for the entire selection.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable cartography covers the whole geographic footprint, but it does not establish the chosen northern opening/valley connection or the selected southern plain-to-playa and inter-playa through-links. These are actual missing source correspondences; a shared valley/basin and modeled continuity are insufficient.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Ione Wash is the western mapped wash. Peavine Creek occupies a separately labelled eastern wash complex in the lower setting. The actual selected terminal is an unnamed southern playa southwest of McLeans, not Millers Pond and not a named river mouth.
records.completion_scope: Four original map views cover all 52 selected parts and the actual southern-playa endpoint. The mapped middle/lower Ione Wash is supported, while the selected northern opening, wash-to-playa extension and inter-playa transfer remain unresolved.
records.supported_name_scope: Direct repeated map labels and the mapped wash corridor support Ione Wash locally. Peavine Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Cloverdale Creek, Golden Wash, Sand Wash, Idlewild Creek and Sunnyside Creek are distinct mapped corridors or tributaries, not interchangeable whole-system names.

scope_limits: The selected northern endpoint is not a verified natural source. Neither adjacent creek labels nor unchannelled valley-floor proximity establishes its link to Ione Wash.
The mapped wetland and sandy wash support broad local corridor correspondence, without demonstrating perennial flow or exact seasonal channel threads.
The two southern playa polygons are observed geographic features, but no displayed lake names or through-channel joining them are established.
The southern plain near Millers Pond lacks a mapped selected through-link; proximity does not establish lake passage.
A single natural-river identity or whole-feature scalar name is unsupported.

records.material_pending_reason: The actual initial waterbody outlet, upper and middle lake/stream transfers, lower selected channel and terminal receiving-water connection remain unresolved at the available original-map scale.
records.completion_scope: All 31 selected parts were considered in four components. The inspected regional location map identifies neighboring lakes and bay, but does not establish the chosen opening, intervening waterbody transfers or actual receiving-water connection.

scope_limits: The chosen opening and each upper and middle lake/stream transfer remain unsupported at practical corridor scale, not merely at exact-bank or endpoint precision.
The lower selected route has regional lake/bay context but its actual final channel-to-receiving-water correspondence is not established. The modeled sea class is not independent terminal evidence.
A lake name, nearby river name, or basin association is not transferred to the whole selected system. Distinct reach/lake names could coexist if later independent correspondence supports them.

NLUIS Armit Lake 56B, Tehery Lake 56C and Chesterfield Inlet 55O were considered but not acquired. A short independent bibliographic search did not establish the precise sheet/project relationship sufficiently beyond the held index and 56G context. They are unrequested leads, not newly failed originals.

Canadian Geoscience Map 459, Bedrock geology, Armit Lake area, was not acquired because its actual project relation to the paused GEM 2 Rae/Tehery-Wager Open File 8149 was unresolved. Different title/year alone was not treated as clearance.

All inherited CanMatrix, CBMT3978, CGN/name-search, NLUIS index/exact-sheet, PCSP2014/coastal-inventory and incompletely identified Nunavut Pitz overview restrictions remain. Incidental restricted-source search results were not opened or used.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
